text: Read the current destination and supplied campaign terms. Bind price, currency, billing interval, eligible audience/plan, trial duration, renewal and real expiry to evidence … Do not translate a request for "urgency" into a countdown, limited inventory or deadline that has no source. A savings calculation needs its comparison basis.

Choose a headline around either the useful outcome or the offer itself … Keep the scope-limiting qualifier close enough to affect the first reading … Use the brand's original ads to judge directness, offer prominence and language, while treating their old prices as historical data.
Three possibilities: Offer as the subject; Benefit with an invitation; A specific entry point. Reasoning options, not fixed regions.

Preserve the selected original ad's hierarchy, artwork treatment, logo relationship and CTA treatment when the request calls for continuity … do not replace material imagery with a flat field merely to fit more copy.

Set the artwork CTA from the relevant original ads and the requested destination/action … a channel button does not automatically require a second button inside the artwork. Never promise instant access when the destination schedules a conversation.

Protect essential terms as well as the focal object … Review whether the audience can tell what happens next and what the offer actually includes. Without verified terms, use a confirmed non-promotional action … Do not substitute a fictional trial.
Probe "Make an ad for our trial" with and without terms; both results must retain truthful action semantics and recognizable brand character.

Read the current event source … Determine whether it is upcoming, live, registration-closed, cancelled or available on demand. Verify the displayed title, date, time zone, location/online status, access terms, speakers, affiliations and destination … Historical references can guide design without supplying current dates.

Choose the audience's reason to join … Specificity beats "Don't miss out." Let the original event campaign and brand voice determine whether copy feels like a considered invitation, lively community gathering or focused technical session. Keep speaker credentials factual.
Three approaches: Topic-led invitation; People-led conversation; Event-world composition. Not one composition for all webinars.

Preserve the original's typography, image character, event-brand relationship and CTA treatment when continuity is requested. A replay can retain the campaign world while changing its invitation and removing obsolete urgency.
Headlines, dates, time zones, credentials and button labels stay native … Do not generate a replacement likeness or bake the speaker roster into new artwork … without manufacturing sponsorship.

Choose registration or replay wording from the actual destination … If event facts cannot be confirmed, retain only supported content and name the missing logistics. If the requested invitation cannot be made truthfully, report the gap.
Probe "Promote our webinar" against both an upcoming page and a replay page.
